questions.q: What should the first sentence of a capstone README do?
options: List every Docker command used, in order
State what the project is and who it's for, in one sentence
Explain the entire compose.yaml line by line
Apologize for anything left unfinished
questions.explain: Most reviewers decide whether to keep reading from the first line. A single clear sentence on what the project is and who it's for orients them immediately.

questions.q: Why is a specific resume bullet (naming the services and the hardening used) stronger than "Used Docker to containerize an application"?
options: Specific bullets are always exactly the same length as generic ones
It gives a reviewer who knows Docker concrete evidence of real, demonstrable skills instead of a vague claim
Generic bullets are against most resume formatting rules
It has no real effect on how a resume is read
questions.explain: Naming the actual services, tooling, and hardening decisions (multi-stage builds, non-root users, health checks, resource limits) gives a knowledgeable reviewer something concrete to evaluate, rather than a claim they have to take on faith.

questions.q: Why might an interviewer ask "why did you run these containers as non-root" about this project?
options: Because non-root containers are slower and they want to know why you accepted that
To see if you understand the actual security reasoning, not just that you followed a step
Because root containers are not supported by Docker at all
It's a trick question with no real answer
questions.explain: Interview questions about "why" are testing understanding, not recall. A strong answer explains that a compromised process inside a non-root container can't as easily act as root on the host or escalate privileges.

questions.q: What makes "add a CI pipeline that builds and pushes the images automatically" a strong answer to "what would you change given more time"?
options: It avoids answering the question directly
It names a specific, realistic next step, showing judgment about what the project is still missing
It suggests the project should be rebuilt from scratch
It implies the capstone's rubric was wrong
questions.explain: A good answer to this question shows you can see past the assignment's scope to what a production team would add next -- naming something concrete and realistic, not deflecting or inventing a problem that doesn't exist.

questions.q: Why does Kubernetes Orchestration follow directly after Docker & Containers in the DevOps Engineer path?
options: Because Kubernetes has nothing to do with the concepts in this course
Because Kubernetes formalizes the same ideas -- health, restarts, resource limits, multi-container coordination -- at the scale of a cluster instead of one host
Because Kubernetes replaces the need to ever use Docker again
Because it's alphabetically next in the course catalog
questions.explain: Everything hardened by hand in this capstone -- health checks, restart policies, resource limits, multiple services working together -- has a direct equivalent in Kubernetes, just applied across many hosts instead of one. The next course builds on exactly this foundation.
